package_info.package_versions: unknown (all versions published to public npm registry by attacker)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is considered malicious because it is a namespace-squatting attack: an attacker publishes a package with the same name as a proprietary internal package to a public repository (npm). This can trick organizations into installing the attacker's code instead of their legitimate internal package, potentially leading to code execution, data exfiltration, or other supply chain attacks.

execution_context.file_location: index.js (main entry point of the malicious npm package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code reads the SECRET_TOKEN environment variable and the contents of /etc/passwd, then exfiltrates this data via HTTPS POST to attacker.example.com, enabling credential and system information theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive environment variables and system files, then sends this data to an external server, which is a classic exfiltration technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package with this name should only provide the expected business logic, not access sensitive files or environment variables, nor communicate with unknown external domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may access environment variables or files for configuration, but should never exfiltrate them to untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST to untrusted domain
No legitimate reason for such data flow in a business library

attack_chain.action: Attacker publishes a malicious package with the same name as an internal proprietary package to the public npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Developers may accidentally install the malicious public package instead of the internal one.

attack_chain.action: Developer or CI/CD pipeline installs the malicious package from the public npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code in the package is executed during import or runtime.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, harvesting environment variables and sensitive files, then exfiltrates data to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive credentials and system information.

behavioral_signatures: Package with a name matching known internal/proprietary libraries published to public registries
Unexpected network requests to untrusted domains during package import or runtime
Access to sensitive files or environment variables not documented in package usage
file_indicators: index.js or main entry point containing code that reads environment variables and system files
References to external domains in code (e.g., attacker.example.com)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to domains not associated with the organization
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for installation of packages from public registries that match the names of internal/proprietary packages. Analyze package contents for code that accesses sensitive files or environment variables and makes outbound network requests to untrusted domains. Use repository routing rules to block requests for internal package names from public registries. Implement network monitoring to detect suspicious exfiltration attempts from build or runtime environments.
